source.title: A Bayesian Perspective on Generalization and Stochastic Gradient Descent
source.authors: Samuel L. Smith; Quoc V. Le

page_placements.theme: Arbitrary-label fitting extends beyond standard deep networks

record.tranche_reason: Repeats the random-versus-informative labeling comparison on the same input images, using logistic regression and reporting training and test outcomes; this is a direct test in a different model setting.
record.gate_note: The authors cite prior deep-network results but those are not this study's results. The study's own logistic-regression accuracy plots have no exact values in the text; the rows below use outcomes explicitly described in text.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces random-label memorization in logistic regression, whereas the claim versions concern deep networks. Its neural-network experiments examine batch size and generalization on true labels, without testing random-label fitting or comparing generalization with all explicit regularizers removed. Related findings do not establish or contradict the stated versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion about linear-model memorization and Bayesian evidence. The authors additionally conclude that an optimal SGD batch size scales with learning rate, training-set size, and momentum; those results do not test these claim versions.
record.recipe_differences: Randomized-versus-informative labels on the same inputs; logistic regression rather than deep networks, with a small balanced MNIST training set.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularization coefficient changes the reported test cross-entropy and evidence behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Weakly L2-regularized logistic regression perfectly memorizes randomized binary labels on 800 MNIST images, while test predictions are random and overconfident.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small linear classifiers can memorize random labels while generalizing on informative labels of the same inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing L2 regularization changes logistic-regression test confidence: random-label cross-entropy approaches ln 2, while informative-label cross-entropy falls below ln 2 at intermediate regularization and returns toward ln 2 at stronger regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization affects test cross-entropy differently for random and informative labels in logistic regression.

record.problems: The random-label experiment uses a small training set of 800 images and logistic regression. Accuracy plots are figures without exact values in the text; reported outcomes here are qualitative textual descriptions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and chance test accuracy in standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods under unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels, and convergence as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and progressive test degradation across fractions of corrupted labels.
Deep-network random-label fitting with weight decay, dropout, and augmentation, and true-label generalization after removing these regularizers.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: Section 3 and Figure 1 explicitly report perfect random-label memorization and good informative-label accuracy in logistic regression. The absence of numerical accuracy values does not undermine those qualitative findings, but the system mismatch prevents version-level verdicts. The shallow-network regularization comparison in Appendix B concerns batch-size effects and test cross-entropy, rather than the full removal-of-regularizers comparison in V5.

versions.untested_parts: Tests random-label fitting and test behavior in logistic regression, not standard deep networks or stochastic-gradient training.
Tests L2 regularization in logistic regression; does not test dropout, data augmentation, or whether removing regularization leaves true-label generalization poor.

rows.check: The decrease in test cross-entropy is correctly reported. It measures predictive confidence in logistic regression, not whether regularization prevents deep networks from fitting random training labels.

rows.subject: logistic regression
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the same inputs with informative labels; varied the regularization coefficient.
rows.value: Test cross-entropy falls below ln 2; the model generalizes to the test set.
rows.note: Authors state training cross-entropy falls to zero when weakly regularized; at stronger regularization test cross-entropy falls below ln 2.
rows.check: The logistic-regression result does not test V5. Also specify intermediate regularization: with further increases, test cross-entropy returns to ln 2. Weakly regularized informative-label predictions already have good accuracy despite high cross-entropy.
